name: Karlskirche Volders
kurzbeschreibung: The Karlskirche Volders near Hall in Tirol: unique oriental-style baroque church designed by Dr. Hippolyt Guarinoni from 1620–1654, featuring six domes and Knoller frescoes.
beschreibung:
Overview

The highly visible Karlskirche in Volders (officially dedicated to St. Karl Borromäus) is picturesquely situated on the southern bank of the Inn River in the Tyrolean Unterinntal, right next to the Hall Ost / Volders motorway exit. As an architectural masterpiece of European significance, this pilgrimage church stands apart from all other sacred buildings in the Alpine region. With its six curved domes, delicate turrets, and exotic silhouette, the church evokes Byzantine basilicas or oriental sacred architecture, captivating art historians and travellers alike.

History & Master Architecture

The church was built on the initiative and visionary plans of the Hall town physician Dr. Hippolyt Guarinoni (1571–1654). Guarinoni, a highly educated polymath and personal physician to the Habsburg noble collegiate ladies in Hall, had vowed the work to the Archbishop of Milan, the canonised Karl Borromäus, whom he had met personally in his youth. The foundation stone was laid on 2 April 1620; despite the devastating turmoil of the Thirty Years' War and plague epidemics, Guarinoni drove the construction forward with his own funds and tireless devotion. Exactly on the day of his death in May 1654, the 83-year-old benefactor witnessed the solemn consecration. The floor plan of the central building is a brilliant architectural achievement: it combines the shape of a Latin cross with a hexagon and is crowned by six tiered drum domes, lending the church its distinctive, almost Venetian-oriental appearance. To secure pastoral care and the long-term preservation of the church, Guarinoni called the mendicant order of the Serviten to Volders, who moved into the adjoining monastery from 1698. The interior was decorated in 1765 by the acclaimed Tyrolean baroque painter Martin Knoller with monumental, colourful ceiling frescoes depicting Karl Borromäus' self-sacrificing life during the Milan plague of 1576. The benefactor Guarinoni found his final resting place directly beneath the steps of the high altar.

Visit & Getting There

The Karlskirche Volders is open daily year-round from approximately 08:00 to 18:30 for visitors. Admission to the church is free of charge (donations for the preservation of this heritage gem are welcome). Arrival by car: directly via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Hall Mitte/Ost – Volders; parking is available in the monastery car park right next to the church. By public transport: from Innsbruck main station or Hall in Tirol railway station, take VVT bus lines 4125 or 4134 directly to the stop Volders Karlskirche (just a few steps from the church portal).

Tips

The forecourt and entrance through the church portal are step-free and fully accessible for wheelchair users and pushchairs. The church is located directly on the famous Inn Cycle Path (R2) and makes an excellent stopover during a cycling tour through the lower Inn valley. Inside the church, take note of the elaborately carved baroque pulpit and the donor plaque commemorating Dr. Guarinoni in the vestibule.
